messages.subject: D-RUG This Thursday!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday (11/6) from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

D-RUG: 10am-noon, DataLab Classroom, Library 360, and zoom https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: Fw: #maptimeDavis: Intro to GIS in R
messages.body_plain:
D-RUG folks who want to work with spatial data might be interested in this week's maptimeDavis workshop by D-RUG's own Elise Hellwig. Details below.

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Specialist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710

Pronouns: she, her, hers
From: geospatial Sympa List (request) <geospatia...@lists.ucdavis.edu> on behalf of Matthew Conner <mco...@ucdavis.edu>
Sent: Monday, November 10, 2025 2:26:34 PM
To: geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [geospatial] #maptimeDavis: Intro to GIS in R

Intro to GIS in R
Date: 11/14/2025
Location: DataLab Classroom - room 360 Shields Library
Description: Intro to GIS in R is a workshop designed to get you started doing Geographic Information Science (GIS) in R. It is, roughly speaking, the R version of  Next Steps in QGIS <https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/Intro-to-Desktop-GIS-with-QGIS/>. We will cover setting up R for GIS, getting data in and out of R, data transformation, filtering, and geoprocessing tools, as well as some basic mapping.
Concepts Covered: R, R Studio, Spatial Data
Speaker:
Elise Hellwig is a Research Data Scientist at the UC Davis DataLab. She has her masters in Agricultural Ecology and has worked on a wide variety of projects from database management, to environmental justice mapping, to text analysis.
Prerequisites: This workshop assumes you have some experience with R. If you are new to R or would like to brush up on your skills, the  DataLab R Basics Reader <https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/workshop_r_basics/> is a great place to start. It also assumes you are familiar with GIS concepts like vectors, rasters, coordinate reference systems etc, which is covered in  Next Steps in QGIS <https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/Intro-to-Desktop-GIS-with-QGIS/>.
Software Required: Bring a laptop with  R <https://ftp.osuosl.org/pub/cran/> and  R Studio <https://posit.co/downloads/> installed. These are free and open source. R is a programming language and R Studio is a tool made by Posit that makes writing R code easier.
RSVP <https://www.eventbrite.com/e/maptimedavis-intro-to-gis-in-r-tickets-1681424408669?aff=oddtdtcreator>

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the  #maptimeDavis YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/@maptimedavis95616>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the  Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s  Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias  mmto...@ucdavis.edu

Matt Conner

Student Services Department

Library

University of California, Davis

on behalf of the #maptimeDavis council
